title: L.A. DOLCE VITA
canon: Neo-noir political drama — ten episodes, ten February days during Carnevale: a presidential candidate caught on a live stream detonates fifteen years of secrets — a journalist's vanished fiancee, his hidden daughter, and the Chigi family's plan to claim her as heir — across a burning Los Angeles, Rome, Venice, and the Arizona Mojave.
look: Found light only — a ranch fireplace, blown-out desert windows, one bare bulb over a boxing ring, a berth lamp and a burning page, canal light, sun through tent canvas; mixed color temperatures and faces that fall into shadow are correct; if a frame reads as a unit publicity still it is wrong.

stills.notes: SCENE CITATION: EP101 Teaser, 'She's Not In Italy' — EXT./INT. PEARL RANCH - FIREPLACE - LATER. Script: 'She's in... the bank, downtown. I held her once.' / 'Emily's hand finds the rosary at her throat. She rips it off and the beads scatter... most into the fire, one bouncing wide to the floorboards.' Why: the engine of the whole season fires in this one grip of hands — the dying lie and the girl it was told to, lit by nothing but the fire the beads are falling into. Emily runs as archetype (70s, delicate frame holding a great deal of iron).
stills.prompt: The front room of a working cattle ranch in Mojave country outside Kingman, Arizona, night, a family wedding thudding on through the barn wall. The only light is the fireplace itself, orange and unsteady on two faces, the rest of the room falling away to black, one thin warm line of party light under the door. A nineteen-year-old all-American girl in a maid-of-honor gown kneels gripping both hands of her grandmother — seventies, delicate frame, the iron just gone out of it, face gray — slumped in an armchair mid-sentence, eyes wide at something past the room. The old woman's fist has just torn the rosary from her own throat: string snapped, beads flying, some already in the flames, one bouncing loose on the floorboards. Wide anamorphic composition, 35mm film still, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: SCENE CITATION: EP101 Act Three, 'Shoebox and Revolver' — INT. KITCHEN, PEARL RANCH - CONTINUOUS. Script: 'Your mother is alive, by God!' / 'He lets her lose to a piece of paper.' / 'Then the tears come, his and hers, and he takes her hand and kisses it.' Why: the resurrection lands not in the words but in the kissed hand — grief for a grandmother, a mother, and the six-year-old who drew a picture for a ghost, all in one frame. Frank runs as archetype (early 70s rancher, ex-Marine bearing).
stills.prompt: The kitchen of the Pearl cattle ranch in Mojave country outside Kingman, Arizona, mid-morning, a funeral wake murmuring behind a closed door. Hard desert sun blows out the window over the sink, flat white glare on copper pots, a small Italian flag and a crucifix on the wall, both faces half in shadow against the burned-out glass. At the farm table an old rancher — early seventies, ex-Marine bearing, black funeral suit, tears on his cheeks — lifts the hand of a nineteen-year-old all-American girl in mourning clothes and kisses it. Around them the aftermath: an old shoebox swept off the table, canceled cashier's checks scattered across the linoleum, one check creased into a wad in her free fist. Her face is wet, furious, and six years old. Wide anamorphic composition, 35mm film still, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: SCENE CITATION: EP101 Act Two, 'The Slim Folder' — INT. MARCELLO'S CABIN - ORIENT EXPRESS - EVENING - MOVING. Script: 'He holds the never-filed column over the open folder, over his mother's snapshot, so the flame will light her face, and touches his lighter to the corner.' / 'In the inch of open door, an eye. KOKO stands in the corridor, dead still, watching the firelight climb his face.' Why: the hinge of the character — the man under the charm, seen by exactly one person, grieving by arson. Koko is only an eye in the dark seam, so she carries no ref here.
stills.prompt: A sleeping cabin aboard the restored Orient Express running north through Italy at night, the door pulled to but not latched, one inch of cold corridor light standing at the seam. Inside, the only other light is a small brass berth lamp and the flame itself: a ruggedly handsome Italian man in his mid-forties, two-day stubble, shirt open at the collar, sits on the made berth holding a burning sheet of typed paper over an open folder, fire crawling toward his fingers, its light climbing his wet eyes while an old snapshot of a woman blackens under the falling ash. In the inch of open door behind him, barely there in the dark, a woman's single eye watches and does not blink. Wide anamorphic composition, 35mm film still, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: SCENE CITATION: EP101 Act Three-B, 'I Will Not, Never' — EXT. BRIDGE, VENEZIA - LATER. Script: 'She looks at it. She does not take it. She folds his own fingers back over it, both her hands around his fist, and holds them closed.' / 'KOKO: Some things you cannot give away.' Why: the whole relationship in one touch — he offers her the last true thing he owns and she closes his hand over it. STAGING FLAG: script plays both masked, lips only; his mask is pushed up here so the cast ref can carry his face — Marco to confirm.
stills.prompt: A small stone footbridge over a side canal in Venice at Carnevale, February night, fog off the water. The light is only what the city gives: one iron lantern on the bridge, the warm far windows of a Grand Canal palazzo smeared through the mist, black water throwing it all back broken. At the parapet a couple stands close — a Korean woman in a baroque ball costume, volto mask above red lips, and a tall Italian man in his mid-forties in a rumpled tuxedo, his mask pushed up into his hair, a bruise starting under one eye. Both her hands are closed around his fist, folding his fingers shut over a small torn strip of newsprint he tried to give away. Wide anamorphic composition, 35mm film still, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: SCENE CITATION: EP101 Act Two, 'Ring and Baby Photo' — INT. BUNGALOW - VENICE BEACH - NIGHT. Script: 'On the bed, Elizabeth's hand drifts up in her sleep, reaching toward the mantle, toward the photograph, and stops in the air, open and empty, the white band of untanned skin bare where the ring sat for twenty years.' Why: Elizabeth's secret told entirely by an unconscious hand — the child she pays for and never contacts, the ring she just gave away. Elizabeth's ref carries face and red hair only, never its painterly style; Maxii runs as archetype (forties, faded star).
stills.prompt: The bedroom of a small bungalow off the Venice Beach boardwalk, Los Angeles, three in the morning. The lamp is off; the only light is the blue-orange flutter of a gas fireplace, and it does not reach the corners. A red-haired woman of about forty sleeps in her evening clothes under a blanket, and her bare hand has drifted up in her sleep, open and empty in the firelight, reaching toward a framed photograph on the mantle of a baby wrapped in a Mexican blanket — the one picture in the room that faces the bed. A pale untanned stripe circles her ring finger. At the bedside a faded-handsome man in his forties bends to fold her hand back down, not yet touching it. Wide anamorphic composition, 35mm film still, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: SCENE CITATION: EP101 Act One, 'Forty-One and Three' — EXT./INT. BOXING RING, TURK'S PLACE - HOLLYWOOD BLVD - NIGHT. Script: 'He sets her down on the canvas, tenderly. Kneels beside her.' / 'TONY: Forty-one and three, in this ring. Right here. You never seen it. Nobody comes here but me.' Why: the Turk's one sacred room and the woman he carried into it — longing offered to someone asleep, the loneliest image in the episode. Tony runs as archetype (31, ex-boxing champ, dark suit).
stills.prompt: A small rundown boxing gym off Hollywood Boulevard, Los Angeles, one in the morning. Every light is off except the single bare bulb over the ring; it drops one hard cone onto the canvas and lets the rest of the gym go to black, heavy bags only shapes at the edge. On the canvas a red-haired woman of about forty in an evening dress lies asleep where she was laid down, shoes still on. A heavyweight in his early thirties, dark suit straining at the shoulders, boxer's ruined hands, kneels beside her inside the cone of light, not touching her, his face caught between pride and pleading — a man showing the only room that ever crowned him to a woman who is not awake to see it. Wide anamorphic composition, 35mm film still, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: SCENE CITATION: EP101 Act Four, staging-tent scene — INT. STAGING TENT, RALLY - EAST L.A. - DAY ('Alone after the rally, Amalia looks at the place on her shoulders where his hands put her in front of the gun'). Script: 'over the bruise she can feel rising under the silk, draws a small target... a circle, a cross through it, two strokes, neat. A map of where she was held.' Why: the quietest, most damning beat of the rally day — a wife privately recording what her husband did with her body, before wiping it away and putting the church face back on. Runs refless; no ruled Amalia cast ref.
stills.prompt: Inside an empty white staging tent behind a campaign rally stage in an East Los Angeles parking lot, late morning. The light is only the sun through the canvas — a flat shadowless glow, the fabric blown bright where the sun hits it, the crowd outside reduced to a wall of moving shadows and dull roar. At a props table with a folding mirror, a poised woman in her early thirties in Sunday-best silk stands alone, chin high, drawing with a lipstick on the shoulder of her own dress: a small neat target, a circle with a cross through it, over the place where her husband's hands held her in front of a gun. Her reflection watches her do it. Wide anamorphic composition, 35mm film still, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: SCENE CITATION: EP101 Act Three, 'Prior Name, Sealed' — INT. PENSIONE ROOM - VENEZIA - NIGHT. Script: 'a creased photograph, a Korean courtroom, a thin man in a defendant's box between two guards, mid-sentence, one hand raised toward a camera he cannot reach' / 'her thumb passes once over the man's raised hand, a habit with years on it.' Why: the antagonist made human in one touch — the hacker alone with the only decoration she travels with, the father behind the whole vendetta.
stills.prompt: A narrow rented room above a side canal in Venice, February night, Carnevale drums faint across the water. One small desk lamp burns; green-black canal light wobbles up through the single window and moves on the ceiling. A young Korean woman with sleek black hair sits at the desk in a silk slip, a black rat tattoo bare on one shoulder, a baroque ball costume hanging pressed on the armoire door behind her. Taped to the wall above the closed laptop is one creased photograph — a thin man in a courtroom defendant's box between two guards, one hand raised toward the camera — and her thumb rests against the raised hand, a habit with years on it. Half her face in lamplight, half gone to dark. Wide anamorphic composition, 35mm film still, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.
